findings.location: Statement, lines 52–56, the paragraph beginning “Equality in claim 1 does not force f to vanish.”
findings.evidence: The paragraph says a nonnegative zero-integral function may be positive at infinitely many points, then ambiguously labels the prose “that is FALSE” before stating that such a function is identically zero. The linked published counterexample fs-nonnegative-integrable-with-zero-integral-vanishes gives Thomae's function, which has integral zero and is positive at every rational point. The assigned consumer's dependency closure reaches this item through thm-aqft-gapped-scalar-forward-positivity → thm-comparison-test-for-improper-integrals → thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral. The used nonnegative-integral subclaim and its proof are sound, so this prose defect is nonfatal.
